key_insight: Four multimodal LLMs relied more on referral wording than MRI evidence when distinguishing glioma from brain abscess.
clinical_relevance: Referral-text sensitivity could undermine AI-assisted brain lesion assessment; this study evaluates diagnostic robustness, not cancer drug discovery.
method: Retrospective single-center study of 60 MRI examinations: 30 gliomas and 30 abscesses.
Paired one axial slice per case with five referral texts and three prompt instructions across four models.
Collected 72,000 responses and compared performance descriptively with two blinded radiologists.
evidence_signal: Changing referral text shifted tumor-call frequency by 79–100 percentage points; model accuracy was 52–73%, versus 78% and 73% for radiologists.
watch_item: Single-slice, single-center testing limits generalizability, and instructions to ignore referral text did not consistently eliminate its influence.
paper_title: Clinical referral text overrides MRI evidence in multimodal large language models: glioma versus brain abscess
